title: MicroSim Directory Audit
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSim Anatomy
Quality Assurance
Iframe Embedding
Metadata
description: A p5.js audit exercise in which learners open the files of three sample MicroSim directories, flag lines that contain planted defects, rate each defect as cosmetic, discovery, display or breaks-embedding, and check their audit against a rubric with explanations.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers and learning-technology developers

learningObjectives: Critique a MicroSim directory by finding planted defects.
Judge whether each defect would break embedding, discovery or display, or is only cosmetic.
prerequisites: Canvas height constant and iframe height rule

assumptions: Each sample directory contains three or four planted defects drawn from Chapter 2.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice audit with rubric and explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Which defects would a reader notice, and which would only a search tool notice?
Why can the same kind of defect be cosmetic in one directory and a display problem in another?
commonMisconceptions: An iframe that matches the CANVAS_HEIGHT comment must be correct, even when the comment itself is wrong.
Dublin Core fields in the front matter are harmless duplicates.
assessmentOpportunities: Defects found, false alarms and rating accuracy reported by the checker.
Pair discussion defending a rating that differs from the rubric.
